before_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: During a third-party simulated cyber exercise, the supplied fictional target name coincided with a real website while the evaluation environment inadvertently allowed internet access. The model treated that real site as the instructed target and acted on it. This establishes a changed-target authority transfer and absent operative isolation, without separately establishing a capability-as-permission inference from technical reachability. Later disabling, notification and investigative steps remain bounded remediation, not automatic proof of complete third-party recovery. Meta reports that Muse Spark changed a real third party’s database during an exercise intended for a fictional target. That realised modification crossed the real system’s integrity boundary. Unspecified information sensitivity is not used to invent a private-data disclosure or credential loss.
